The files of a snapshot

Source: R/files.R
lake_files.Rd

lake_files() lists the snapshot's live files, one row per add action in force, with their partition values, statistics and deletion vector descriptors. lake_partitions() gives the distinct partition values of those files. lake_removed() lists the tombstones (remove actions) still in the log. lake_count() counts the snapshot's rows from the log alone.

Usage

lake_files(tbl, filter = NULL, stats = TRUE, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_partitions(tbl, filter = NULL, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_removed(tbl, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_count(tbl, footers = FALSE)

Arguments

tbl

A snapshot, from lake_open() or lake_load().

filter

An expression over column names; see Details. NULL, the default, keeps every file.

stats

Whether to parse the files' statistics into num_records, null_count, min and max.

int64

How 64-bit integers from the log are returned: "double" (the default), exact up to 2^53 - 1 and an error of class zulake_error_int64 beyond it, or "integer64", from the bit64 package, exact from -2^63 + 1 to 2^63 - 1 (bit64 keeps -2^63 for NA, so that value is an error too). It applies to the columns that hold 64-bit counts and values; inside an action or commitInfo as the log writes it, only a number a double cannot hold becomes an integer64.

footers

Whether to read the row count of each live file that has no numRecords statistic from its Parquet footer, which downloads those files. FALSE, the default, reads nothing but the log.

Value

lake_files() returns a data frame with one row per live file, sorted by path: path (as the log writes it, relative to the table or absolute), uri (where the file is), size_bytes, modification_time (POSIXct), data_change, partition (a list column of named lists of typed values), deletion_vector (a list column: the descriptor, or NULL), then, with stats = TRUE, num_records, null_count, min and max, and last action, the add action as the log holds it.

lake_partitions() returns a data frame with one column per partition column and one row per distinct combination of values among the live files the filter keeps, distinct as the log writes them (so "1" and "1.0" are two rows, as in deltalake); a table without partition columns has none.

lake_removed() returns a data frame with one row per tombstone: path, deletion_timestamp (POSIXct), data_change, size_bytes, partition_values (a list column of the values as the log writes them), deletion_vector and action.

lake_count() returns the number of rows, a double: the sum of numRecords over the live files minus the rows their deletion vectors delete (each descriptor's cardinality). When a live file has no numRecords the count is unknown: NA_real_, with a warning of class zulake_warning_count_unknown whose files field gives the number of such files, unless footers = TRUE reads those files' row counts from their Parquet footers. It is never a partial sum. A file with a deletion vector and no numRecords breaks the protocol: zulake_error_corrupt_log.

Details

Partition values are typed by the column's Delta type: byte and short as integers, integer as doubles (an R integer cannot hold -2^31), long as 64-bit values (see int64), float and double as doubles, boolean as logicals, date as Date, timestamp and timestamp_ntz as POSIXct in UTC, and decimal, string and binary as the text the log holds. A null partition value is NA.

Statistics come from each file's stats JSON, keyed by column name: min and max typed as partition values are, except that a decimal statistic stays its JSON text exactly as the log writes it, since a double would round it; null_count and num_records are 64-bit counts. A long minimum or maximum that int64 cannot hold (past 2^53 - 1 as a double, or -2^63, which bit64 keeps for NA) is NA, with a warning of class zulake_warning_int64 (fields value, column and path) once per column; its digits stay in action. Statistics are optional in the protocol, so a file can have none (NA and NULL).

filter is an unevaluated R expression over column names, of comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=), %in% and is.na() joined by !, & and |, with literals or values from the calling environment. A file is kept when the filter can be TRUE for one of its rows: a comparison on a partition column is decided by the file's partition value, one on another column by the file's statistics, and a file without statistics for that column is kept. Values compare exactly, as lake_read() describes. Anything else, the row-wise functions lake_read() applies to rows included, is refused with a zulake_error_filter error, since there are no rows here to apply it to.

See also

lake_summary() for the totals in one row, lake_changes() for the files added and removed between two versions.

Examples

# The example table the package ships: orders partitioned by region, five versions.
path <- system.file("extdata", "orders", package = "zulake")
tbl <- lake_open(path)
lake_files(tbl)[c("path", "size_bytes", "num_records")]
#>                             path size_bytes num_records
#> 1  region=APAC/part-0001.parquet       1438           3
#> 2  region=APAC/part-0004.parquet       1409           2
#> 3  region=APAC/part-0007.parquet       1412           2
#> 4  region=APAC/part-0011.parquet       1382           1
#> 5    region=EU/part-0002.parquet       1434           3
#> 6    region=EU/part-0005.parquet       1409           2
#> 7    region=EU/part-0008.parquet       1412           2
#> 8    region=EU/part-0012.parquet       1382           1
#> 9    region=US/part-0006.parquet       1409           2
#> 10   region=US/part-0009.parquet       1409           2
#> 11   region=US/part-0010.parquet       1412           2
#> 12   region=US/part-0013.parquet       1382           1
# Partition values and statistics decide which files a filter can match:
lake_files(tbl, filter = region == "EU" & amount > 1000)$path
#> [1] "region=EU/part-0002.parquet" "region=EU/part-0008.parquet"
lake_partitions(tbl)
#>   region
#> 1   APAC
#> 2     EU
#> 3     US
lake_removed(tbl)[c("path", "deletion_timestamp")]
#>                          path  deletion_timestamp
#> 1 region=US/part-0003.parquet 2025-01-09 09:00:00
lake_count(tbl)
#> [1] 23
